messages:
jon: Heads-up — monitoring flagged us-west1 GPU pool at 98% (p100). Cluster-autoscaler started provisioning but we're hitting regional soft quota and some pods are pending (~200 across inference-prod batch + realtime). Thinking we should do a cross-cluster rebalance with weighted routing and a warm-pool spin-up. Anyone on call can weigh in? :eyes:
infra-bot: autoscaler event: `ScaleUp: 12 nodes requested, 0 fulfilled due to quota`
infra-bot: quota api response: `{\n  \"region\": \"us-west1\",\n  \"available_gpus\": 8,\n  \"requested_gpus\": 64\n}`
maya: I can take this. Quick notes: prefer warm-pool spin-up in us-west2 first (closer -> lower latency) and then route lower-priority pods there. For realtime we should avoid >50ms p95 penalty.
maya: Can we do weighted routing at the load-balancer level for queue consumers? If not, use node-affinity + failover label and let the queue broker reassign.
rachel: +1 on warm-pool. Also we need to honor taints/tolerations so critical inference doesn't land on preemptible warm nodes unless we mark them tolerated. Suggest policy: critical pods -> reserved nodes in us-west1; spill -> warm/preemptible in us-west2/us-central1.
jon: Good. Cost note: preemptible warm pools reduce cost but risk churn; we should trace model fallbacks to quantized variants if latency jumps.
tom: Cross-region fallback will add egress and latency. If we route model >50ms to another region, degrade model size (quantize/half-precision) first. We should instrument a latency budget per route.
sophie: I can push a quick config to capacity-broker to probe target clusters and switch routing weight. Patch example:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: capacity-broker-config
data:
  weights: |
    us-west1: 0.6
    us-west2: 0.3
    us-central1: 0.1
```
and command to reload: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/capacity-broker -n infra`
jon: Nice. Also let's add an autoscaler override to reduce scale-down aggressiveness while warm pools spin: `kubectl patch vmware-autoscaler -n infra --type merge -p '{"spec":{"scaleDown":{"enabled":false}}}'` — only for the temp window.
maya: I'll start warm-pool create in us-west2 now. ETA ~6m. I'll mark the warm nodes with label `warmpool=true` and taint `warm=true:NoSchedule` so only spill jobs tolerate.
rachel: I'll update the inference routing rules to prefer model-quantized variants for cross-region spill. Quick snippet: `env MODEL_FALLBACK=quantized` in the consumer config.
tom: Monitoring checklist: update SLO graph to show cross-region p95 and egress cost delta. Also add an alert if cross-region p95 > 80ms.
jon: Action items: maya -> spin warm pool (in progress), sophie -> apply capacity-broker weights (after maya), rachel -> flip model fallback envs, tom -> update dashboards + alert, i'll own rollback and postmortem if needed.
sophie: Applied temporary capacity-broker weights (staged). Will not flip traffic until warm nodes are Ready.
infra-bot: cluster event: `nodes added: 10 in us-west2 (warm-pool)`
maya: Warm nodes ready. Label/taint applied. Starting gradual spill of batch queues.
jon: Starting a 10-min canary: shifting 15% of non-critical queue traffic to us-west2. Watch latency + errors.
rachel: Canary looks stable for first 2m. p95 realtime unchanged, batch throughput up.
tom: Egress looks low so far. Cost projection for next 24h +5% if warm preemptible used, +12% if we keep reserved in multiple regions.
jon: OK keep canary for 30m. If stable we'll bump to 40% and let autoscaler finish provisioning. After that revert scaleDown settings.
sophie: Noted. I'll add a short-lived runbook entry in #help for on-call steps for similar events.
maya: thanks — will follow up with exact command list in the runbook.
jon: Good work team. Postmortem/learnings queued if we end up with cross-region penalties. For now this looks like the right lowest-cost path with reduced disruption. :thumbsup:
